children.label: See a signal 10x above the XLZD limit?

notes.what: IceCube-Gen2 is a cubic-kilometre-scale ice detector at the South Pole that records the energy of muon tracks made by neutrinos; pointed at the Sun it can measure the energy spectrum, not just the flux, of neutrinos from dark matter annihilating in the solar core. The mean neutrino energy tags the annihilation channel: heavy mediators decaying to quarks and taus give a hard spectrum near half the dark-matter mass, while GeV-scale Z' bosons decay to muons and pions that stop in the Sun before decaying, leaving few high-energy neutrinos. All these regions already predict a flux at the Gen2 limit, so the spectral shape is the natural next handle.
notes.reasoning: Hard regions annihilate to Z' with MZp 45-990 GeV whose decays to b/c/tau produce nu with <E> ~ MDM/4 ~ 100-175 GeV (MDM 320-710). Soft regions have MZp 1-6 GeV: Z' decays to mu/pi that range out in the solar core, suppressing E_nu > 100 GeV by orders of magnitude; only a soft secondary component survives.
notes.feasibility: IceCube-Gen2 itself; muon-track energy resolution ~30 percent, sufficient for a hard/soft discrimination with ~20-50 signal events at the flux this leaf already implies; dominant systematic is the atmospheric-neutrino background in the solar cone.

notes.what: LHCb and the B-factories (BaBar, Belle II) look for the dark U(1)' Z' boson produced in collisions through its small kinetic mixing epsilon with the photon, decaying to an electron or muon pair that appears as a narrow bump in the dilepton mass spectrum. It is most sensitive for Z' masses between 0.2 and 70 GeV with epsilon above about 1e-3. Our catalog only recasts the heavy-mass dilepton search, so this low-mass visible search directly tests the (MZp, epsilon) values that differ by orders of magnitude between these regions.
notes.reasoning: Seen regions have MZp 1-50 GeV with epsilon 1e-3 to 0.1 (e.g. R4: 18-42 GeV at eps 0.04-0.1; R6: 1 GeV at eps 4e-3 to 0.1), well inside LHCb prompt reach (eps~1e-3 at tens of GeV, ~2e-4 at 1 GeV). Not-seen regions have eps <~ 1e-4 (R3, R8, R12: eps <= 1e-5 at 1-8 GeV) or MZp>70 GeV (R7: 986 GeV; R14/R15: ~560 GeV). R0/R1 straddle the cut but contain decisively visible corners.

notes.reasoning: Secluded annihilation SS*->Z'Z' gives sigma_v = 2.3e-19 g'^4/m_DM^2 cm^3/s. Regions with gU1p 0.33-0.51 and m_Z'<m_DM predict 1.4-3.3e-26 cm^3/s (R2: g'=0.431,m=640 -> 2.0e-26; R14/R15: g'=0.514,m=704 -> 3.3e-26), at the CTA GC cascade reach. Regions with gU1p 0.018-0.15 predict 1e-31 to 2e-28 cm^3/s, six orders below. R7 has m_Z'=986 GeV > m_DM=546 GeV so the channel is shut. Marginal: leaf R0 spans gU1p 0.036-0.42 and genuinely straddles the cut; assigned by log-midpoint 0.12.

notes.what: IceCube-Gen2 measures the energy spectrum of muon neutrinos coming from dark-matter annihilation in the Sun's core. Annihilation into heavy Z' bosons gives a hard neutrino spectrum, while GeV-scale Z' decay products stop in the Sun and yield only soft neutrinos, so the mean energy tags which mediator mass range a region lives in.
notes.reasoning: 27 regions have MZp >= ~35 GeV (117-583 GeV in R4, 550 GeV family, 986 GeV in R0) -> <E_nu> ~ 100-175 GeV. 13 regions have MZp 1-5 GeV -> stopped mu/pi, <E_nu> << 100 GeV. Flux is already at 1-10x the Gen2 limit, so spectrometry is statistics-limited but feasible.
notes.feasibility: IceCube-Gen2; ~30 percent track-energy resolution; needs tens of solar events, dominant systematic is atmospheric-nu background.

This directly probes the Z' mass and mixing epsilon, the two parameters that vary most across these regions and that the catalog's heavy-dilepton recast does not cover below ~100 GeV.
notes.reasoning: Visible: R1 (17-41 GeV, eps 0.011-0.1), R7, R49 (24-34 GeV, eps 0.05-0.1), R33/R34 (1 GeV, eps 3e-3 to 1e-2), etc. Invisible: the 550-GeV family (R13,R20,R22-R27,R44-R47) and R0 (986 GeV) are above the mass range; R3, R18, R30, R36-R38, R50 have eps <= 1e-4 at GeV masses, far below reach.

notes.feasibility: IceCube-Gen2; ~30 percent energy resolution; tens of events at this leaf's flux; atmospheric background dominates.

notes.what: A proposed 100 TeV proton collider (FCC-hh) would extend the search for heavy neutral bosons decaying to electron or muon pairs far beyond the LHC. A multi-TeV Z' with kinetic mixing of 0.1 is produced copiously there. Only one region in this group has such a heavy, strongly mixed Z'.
notes.reasoning: R1: MZp 2-2.8 TeV with eps=0.1 -> effective coupling ~0.03e gives sigma x BR ~ 0.1-1 fb at 100 TeV, observable with ab-level luminosity. R2-R4 have MZp 1-22 GeV with eps <= 1e-4: nothing at high mass.
notes.feasibility: FCC-hh design (formally proposed); dilepton mass resolution ~1 percent; needs no improvement over design sensitivity; PDF/luminosity systematics subdominant.

children.label: Ultra-luminosity low-mass dimuon scan dimuon peak ~22 GeV, epsilon

notes.what: A far higher-statistics version of the LHCb dark-photon dimuon search, scanning for a very faint narrow muon-pair peak near 22 GeV. Sensitivity to the mixing parameter improves with the square root of luminosity, so reaching epsilon of a few 1e-5 needs orders of magnitude more data than planned. It would tag the one region with epsilon ~7e-5.
notes.reasoning: R2 has MZp 22 GeV, eps 6.8-8.5e-5; R3 (10 GeV) and R4 (1 GeV) have eps = 1e-6, unreachable by any conceivable luminosity. Drell-Yan dimuon background under a 22 GeV peak is the limiting systematic.
notes.feasibility: Closest: LHCb Upgrade II (eps reach ~3e-4 at 20 GeV); required improvement ~5x in eps, ~25x in eps^2 i.e. ~600x luminosity-equivalent; background-model systematics likely saturate first.

notes.what: A direct-detection experiment like XLZD/DARWIN records the energy of each nuclear recoil; for dark matter lighter than the xenon nucleus the shape of that energy spectrum depends strongly on the particle's mass, so a fit to the spectrum measures the mass. Since this leaf already implies a signal at 1-10x the XLZD limit, the same detector that counts the events can weigh the particle. That splits the 68-GeV region from the 94-95 GeV family.
notes.reasoning: R0 has MDM 67.5-69.8 GeV; R1-R4 have 94-95 GeV. Both are below the Xe target mass (~122 GeV), the regime of maximal spectral sensitivity; with O(50-100) events (sigma_SI at 1-10x XLZD) published projections give ~15-20 percent mass resolution, cleanly separating 68 from 95 GeV.

notes.what: A purpose-built high-rate spectrometer in the forward region of an LHC interaction point, recording enormous samples of muon pairs to hunt for an extremely faint narrow resonance between 10 and 30 GeV. It probes kinetic mixing an order of magnitude below current dimuon searches. Only one region here has a Z' bright enough for even this instrument.
notes.reasoning: R0 predicts eps = 1.3-1.9e-4 at MZp ~ 21 GeV — visible if the eps reach is pushed to 1e-4; R1+R2 predict eps = 1e-6 at 1-1.7 GeV, invisible to any collider search. R1 vs R2 differ only in MZp (1.6 vs 1.1 GeV) and dark couplings and remain degenerate.
notes.feasibility: Closest: LHCb Upgrade II (eps ~ 3e-4 prompt at 20 GeV); required ~3x in eps = ~10x in rate beyond Upgrade II; dominant systematic is the smooth Drell-Yan continuum shape under the peak.

notes.what: All three regions have nearly the same dark-matter mass (92-95 GeV) and a Z' whose mixing with the photon is at or below 1.3e-4, out of reach of every published or formally projected visible or invisible dark-photon search at these masses (1.6-21 GeV). No planned measurement discriminates them.
notes.reasoning: R0: MZp 20.8 GeV, eps 1.3e-4 — a factor ~8 below LHCb Upgrade prompt reach at that mass; R1/R2: MZp 1-1.7 GeV, eps 1e-6 — five hundred times below B-factory reach. Masses (92 vs 95 GeV) are too close for a recoil-spectrum fit at this event count.

notes.what: Observations of colliding galaxy clusters and the shapes of dark-matter halos constrain how often dark-matter particles scatter off each other. The dark quartic couplings that distinguish these regions directly set this self-scattering rate. It is the only physical observable in which the regions differ at all.
notes.reasoning: Regions with a quartic near 10 (R0,R2,R4-R12) predict sigma/m ~ 4e-7 cm^2/g at MDM = 5 GeV; R1 and R3 (quartics <~ 1.5) predict <~ 1e-9. Both are ~5 orders below current astrophysical sensitivity (~0.1-1 cm^2/g), so this is a statement of principle, not practice — the degeneracy is physically real.
notes.feasibility: Closest: cluster-merger lensing constraints (sigma/m ~ 0.1-1 cm^2/g); required improvement >1e5; dominant systematic is baryonic-physics modeling of halo shapes.

notes.what: All 13 regions sit at the same dark-matter mass (about 5 GeV), same Z' mass (1-2 GeV), same gauge coupling, and mixing below every search's reach; they differ only in the dark sector's internal self-couplings (the alpha2-alpha6 quartics), which control how dark particles scatter off each other but produce no laboratory signal. No published or planned measurement distinguishes them.
notes.reasoning: eps <= 1.8e-4 at 1-2 GeV is ~5x below even B-factory single-photon reach for a visibly decaying Z'; MDM spread (4.6-5.6 GeV) is within recoil-fit resolution. The alpha2-alpha6 differences (0.001 vs 10) affect only DM-DM scattering.

This weighs the particle and separates the ~70-GeV family of regions from the ~96-GeV family.

notes.what: CRESST-III operates cryogenic scintillating crystals with energy thresholds near 30 eV, low enough to detect the tiny nuclear recoils from GeV-mass dark matter. The maximum recoil energy is set by kinematics and grows with the dark-matter mass, so measuring where the spectrum ends weighs the particle. That separates the 1-GeV region from the 2.2-GeV region.
notes.reasoning: On a tungsten target the recoil endpoint is ~75 eV for MDM = 1 GeV (R0) vs ~350 eV for 2.2 GeV (R1) at the galactic escape velocity — one side below, the other well above a 150 eV cut within CRESST-III's demonstrated range. Both regions have a Higgs-portal coupling (alpha1 ~ 0.004) large enough for a detectable rate.

Measuring that endpoint weighs the particle and separates the heavy regions from the light ones.
